problem: Most Vision-and-Dialogue Navigation work uses human-annotated dialogue only as input and does not generate it. The few interactive methods rely on templates, yes/no questions, or ask at fixed intervals, so agents cannot decide when and what to ask.
motivation: An agent that can ask an oracle for help when unsure, and receive informative answers, is a step toward conversational, human-in-the-loop navigation. This needs three abilities at once: deciding when to ask, generating the question, and answering it from the path to the goal.
key_idea: Combine a DUET navigator with a multimodal GPT-2 dialogue model that generates free-form question-answer pairs, triggered by a learnable entropy threshold on the navigator's action distribution.
insight: Conditioning the oracle's answer on future images along the shortest path and on the target object improves answer quality (CIDEr 0.111 without future images, 0.145 without target object, 0.179 with both). A learned entropy threshold gives the best goal progress (13.35) among the fixed thresholds tried (0.9/1.0/1.1), although fixed-interval triggering gives better SR/SPL on CVDN. Synthetic dialogues used as augmentation help NDH navigation.
method: Dialogue model: GPT-2 (12 layers, d=768, 124M) fine-tuned on CVDN with image features (ResNet-152 frontal 60° crops), sequence [target, current image, question, future images t..t+k, answer], plus position and segment embeddings
Question/answer generation: the question is conditioned only on the current view and the target object; the answer also uses k=20 future images along the Dijkstra shortest path to the goal
Navigator: DUET (dual-scale graph Transformer) modified to allow backtracking (only the current node is masked), with a global action space over all graph nodes plus STOP
Learnable prompt embeddings: prepended in place of an instruction, since CVDN gives only the target object
Entropy-triggered dialogue: when the entropy of the action distribution exceeds a threshold α, the QA pair is generated and concatenated to the navigator input, and the action is recomputed

Learnable threshold: α̂ is trained with a BCE loss so that entropy is above α̂ at nodes where the dataset has dialogue, only during teacher-forcing; fixed-interval (4/5/6 steps) triggers are alternatives
NDH augmentation: QA pairs are generated for every training trajectory and DUET is trained on the doubled dataset

setting.backbone: DUET navigator (164M, fine-tuned) + GPT-2 dialogue model (124M, fine-tuned); ResNet-152 features
setting.training_data: CVDN / NDH training splits (2050 trajectories, 7K NDH episodes); NDH augmented with self-generated synthetic dialogues (dataset doubled)
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (navigator) plus frontal 60° crops (dialogue model)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (all nodes in the graph plus STOP)
setting.privileged: The oracle (dialogue model's answer) uses future images along the GT shortest path to the goal, and the target object label is given

numbers_note: CVDN metrics were printed on val-unseen only. The text says 'SR of 7.73 and SPL of 9.62' for the 5-step variant, but the table shows SPL 7.73 and SR 9.62. The table values are used. NDH is not in the canonical benchmark list, so it is tagged other:NDH. NDH SPL/SR are printed as percentages (e.g. 49, 60).
results: On CVDN val-unseen, the learnable-threshold UNMuTe reaches goal progress 13.35 m, beating SCoA (11.19) and RMM (8.9). Triggering every 5 steps gives the best SR/SPL (9.62/7.73). On NDH it beats HAMT: Player gets GP 5.88 on val-unseen and 5.75 on test-unseen (HAMT 5.13 and 5.58), and Planner gets SR 60 / SPL 49 on val-unseen.
limitations: Success rates on interactive CVDN are low (SR at most about 12) and SPL/SR vary a lot across trigger settings and prompt counts, so there is no single best configuration

Answers rely on the shortest path and future images, so it is a simulated oracle rather than a human. Question quality is much lower than answer quality (CIDEr 0.181 for questions, 0.179 for answers, with low BLEU and other scores), and human-in-the-loop use is left to future work
Competitor comparisons are partial: RMM and SCoA report only GP on CVDN, and the NDH baselines use different training regimes
